parts.text: Which claim is correct about how the interest is calculated?

options.text: Each year the interest is $5\%$ of the same principal $\mathrm{Rs}\,6000$.
Each year the interest is $5\%$ of the amount after adding the previous year's interest.
Simple interest uses the $5\%$ rate in year $1$ only, then the principal earns nothing.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Eklavya deposits $\mathrm{Rs}\,6000$ at $5\%$ per year simple interest for $4$ years.

part_answers.answer: Without compounding the principal stays fixed, so each year's interest is 5% of the same Rs 6000; over 4 years interest totals 4×0.05×6000=Rs 1200.

teacher.key_rationale: Simple interest keeps the principal fixed each term. Compounding would grow the base; shutting off the rate after year 1 is outside the simple-interest hinge.
